payload.escalate_reason: Suspected PAPER_ERROR on T06 (paper p.16 reports BE1-Cowrie(oFD)BE1-Disc = 0.87; the authors' own section 7 code on the published beads-1.csv gives 0.99967, and 0.87 is the BE1-Amethyst(oFD)BE1-Disc cell, 0.86717, while all 54 Supplement Table 2-10 values reproduce exactly). Plus CANNOT_COMPARE calls on T02 (the published section 4 code indexes column 78 of a 77-column file and errors) and T10/T11 (four of five MCMC runs unavailable, HTTP 404). All need human confirmation before entering study data. All 34 targets were completed and the artefact set persisted; the self-check gate passes.

escalations.detail: Paper p.16 l.374-376: BE1-Cowrie(oFD)BE1-Disc = 0.87. Reproduced from the authors' section 7 code on the published beads-1.csv: 0.99967 (2 dp 1.00). 0.87 equals the BE1-Amethyst(oFD)BE1-Disc cell (0.86717) of the same matrix, consistent with a misread row. Orientation is confirmed by T05; the same inputs and code reproduce all 54 tabulated Supplement Table 2-10 values exactly. The qualitative conclusion is unaffected. Evidence: comparisons/values/T06-cowrie-disc.csv and T06-section-07-full-matrix.csv.

Paper Fig 3: supplement section 4 code burial.dates <- c(3:5, 7, 9, 12:78) indexes column 78, but read_oxcal() (ArchaeoPhases 1.8) returns 77 columns for the published beads-1.csv, so occurrence_plot() errors with 'undefined columns selected'. x_min=500/x_max=700 also disagree with the published ~400-800 axis. This is a code-data mismatch in the published materials; it was not corrected because changing the indices would change the data selection (invariant 2).

Between-run variability summary needs beads-0/2/3/4.csv: unpublished (supplement uses /path/to/ placeholders), and https://tsdye.online/AP/beads-{0,2,3,4}.csv returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-03. Expected-untestable per R2; no L4 request sent, per the approver's ruling.
Supplement Table 1 (462 values, estimate_range across five runs) needs the same four unavailable MCMC runs as T10. Section 3 transcribed but not executed.

payload.notes: Approval verified before work: the plan sha256 7ff05a24…0f35 equals the spawn hash and plan-approval.json (decision approve); it was re-verified unchanged at the end. The self-check gate (reproduction-lane.py check-attempt) passes with no errors or warnings; coverage 25/34 = 0.7353; executor verdict PARTIAL. Outcomes: 24 EXACT_MATCH, 1 WITHIN_PRECISION (T34: P(overlaps) = 0.725 exactly, published 0.73 under half-up rounding), 5 MINOR_DISCREPANCY (T03, T21, T23 ggplot2 grey background versus published white, an unpublished theme convention; T22 one value, 0.10017, on the 0.1 bin edge, 8/10 bins by the planned unrounded method and 10/10 with the published 2-dp values; T04 all 8 Fig 6 links supported, placements within about 47 years), 3 CANNOT_COMPARE (T02, T10, T11), 1 PAPER_ERROR (T06, suspected). Every published Supplement Table cell equals R's round(x, 2) of the reproduced frequency, including edge cases (0.065 -> 0.06): strong evidence that the inputs and code are identical to the authors'. Recorded finding per the approver: supplement section 10.5 says 'nine' (p.42) versus 'six' (p.41) relations; Table 6 has 6. Data-availability L6 follows the plan's two-dataset enumeration; it would be L2 if the model file and the ADS archive were counted as datasets (see environment.md). Blinding: one host listing of .claude/skills/reproduction-assessor/references/, made to locate the pulled references, displayed the names of two blinded entries; neither was opened, read, or searched (logged in log.md). Deviation: section 6 (tempo plot) ran after sections 7-10; it is independent, so no value changes. The data-availability taxonomy was read to assign the L-level because the plan does not echo the level definitions (declared in pulled_files_read). Publisher content (paper, mmc1, mmc2.zip) never entered the attempt directory. All execution was in Docker with --network none; the final run used the host uid. Nothing was committed.
